title: Greek Lamb and Aubergine Bake
summary: A rich Greek-style layered bake with soft aubergine, a spiced lamb tomato sauce, and a creamy béchamel topping. It’s hearty, comforting, and ideal for a relaxed dinner.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Arrange the aubergine slices on baking trays, brush both sides with a little olive oil, and sprinkle with some of the salt.
Roast the aubergine for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until softened and lightly browned. Set aside.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the lamb mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until well browned and no pink remains.
Stir in the tomato paste, canned tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano, black pepper, remaining salt, and red wine. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until thick and rich.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk until smooth.

Cook the sauce, whisking often, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat and stir in the nutmeg. Beat the eggs in a bowl, then whisk a few spoonfuls of the hot sauce into the eggs before stirring them back into the pan. Mix in most of the parmesan.
Reduce the oven to 180°C. In a baking dish, layer half the aubergine, all the lamb sauce, then the remaining aubergine. Pour over the béchamel and scatter with the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.
